newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian Ventspils port optimistic on 1997.
newsitem.headline: Latvian Ventspils port optimistic on 1997.

text.p: Latvia's Ventspils port, an important outlet for Russian transit goods, expects to beat Soviet-era highs in cargo turnover in 1997, the port said on Wednesday.

The ice-free port on Latvia's west coast registered 35.7 million tonnes of cargo last year, a 20 percent rise against 1995. Ventspils said this made it the biggest port by far on the Baltic Sea coast.

"The pace at which volumes have grown during recent years allows us to forecast that during its centenary year of 1997 Ventspils port will beat its record turnover of 38.1 million tonnes of 1983," the port said in a statement.
Some 80 percent of Latvian transit business goes through Ventspils, which has been granted the status of a free-port.
Transit services were the main factor behind Latvia's 1996 GDP growth, estimated at 2.5 percent against a fall of 1.6 percent in 1995.
Russian crude, oil products and metal cargoes are on the increase in Ventspils.
It reloaded 27.3 million tonnes of crude and oil products in 1996, an increase of 6.2 million tonnes against 1995.
An all-time high of 2.3 million tonnes of metal cargoes was registered in Ventspils last year.
The port said that the amount of cargo it handled last year was five million tonnes more than the amount handled at Estonian and Lithuanian ports together.
It said that this put among Europe's top 20 ports.
